title: Agent orchestration
intro: Rules for a lead agent that runs sub-agents, and for unattended agents. Each rule has a stable id; turn one off with `forge orchestration off <id>` (per repo, or --global), then `forge sync`.

rules.text: Start long commands (test suites, builds, e2e runs) in the background and wait for the completion signal. Never write sleep or poll loops; read results with `tail`/`grep`, not by re-reading whole logs.
rules.rationale: Every poll re-reads the agent's whole context. In the session behind this pack, agents waiting on a shared lock polled every ~10 minutes against a 250–300k-token context: one agent ran 506 turns for ~5k output tokens.

rules.text: Run at most {parallelCap} agents in parallel, and never more than the scarcest shared resource (test environment, ports, database, CI runners) can serve at once. Queue the rest.
rules.rationale: Agents beyond what the shared resource can serve do no work; they wait, and waiting agents re-read their context. Seven agents on one e2e environment mostly queued.

rules.text: Run full e2e and integration suites in CI. Locally, run only fast checks (typecheck, lint, unit tests of the code you touched) before pushing.
rules.rationale: A heavy suite on a shared local environment serialises every agent behind it. CI runners queue the work without holding an agent's context open.

rules.text: Give each sub-agent one small task and a fresh context. Hand back a concise report (what changed, checks run, open items), not a transcript.
rules.rationale: A small fresh context is cheap to re-read; a long one is re-read on every turn. A concise report keeps the lead's context small too.

rules.text: Pick each agent's model with `forge route "<task>" --json` (add `--mode unattended` for agents nobody watches). Never start at the top tier by default.
rules.rationale: Hand-picking the most expensive tier for routine work cost ~140M tokens in one session. Routing picks the cheapest capable tier, with floors for risky work.

rules.text: Changes touching money, auth, secrets, migrations or security ship with tests in the same change and a lead review of the diff. UI-only tests may follow later.
rules.rationale: Cheaper routing must not lower quality where mistakes are costly: a double-charge race in payment code was caught only by a lead reviewing the money diff.

rules.text: If local e2e is unavoidable, serialise it behind a lock or give each agent its own ports and database.
rules.rationale: Agents sharing one environment overwrite each other's state, and the resulting flaky failures look like real bugs.

rules.text: As lead, keep replies to completion notifications short and do not re-read large files or logs; read the sub-agent's report.
rules.rationale: The lead's context is re-read on every notification; each large file it pulls in is paid for again on every later turn.
